_comment: f4d-kit opting ITSELF in to its own plugin-declared hooks (A18). This file's presence is the whole signal hook_opted_in() checks (hooks/_parse.sh) — without it, this repo's own guard.sh/rule-zero.sh/etc. would go dark the moment hooks/hooks.json shipped, because those scripts are the SAME files this repo's .claude/settings.json already wires by relative path. That direct settings.json wiring stays (it is what makes this repo's own hooks the one case that worked before A18 was fixed, per the _comment there), so the two now overlap deliberately: same shape as guard.sh + guard-local.sh double-wiring, which A6 proved safe (any exit-2 blocks regardless of order). The accepted cost is specific to this repo's own dev sessions only: guard.sh etc. run twice per matched tool call, and a real deny logs two .enforcement-log lines instead of one. No scaffolded target repo pays that cost — it gets exactly one wiring path, the plugin's global hooks.json. version/files stay empty because this repo has no .claude/rules/ of its own to track (templates/rules/ is the SOURCE others copy from, not a target of scripts/upgrade.py's diffing).
